recent.commitMessage:
docs: close out the audit — nothing filed on the day is still open

The "Still open" table was written when four of its rows were mine to do. They
are done, so it now says so, and the two that remain are genuinely Ben's: the
Google Cloud TTS billing switch he shares with WordZoo, and the six needs_review
rows that only a person with a real phone can answer.

The 28 React Compiler lint errors are deliberately NOT a CRM row. They are all
one rule, none is a live bug, and fixing them is a refactor of most of the
interactive components — a row for them would sit on the board being true and
never actionable, which is the thing this audit was written to stop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(daily-card): the email went silent instead of saying anything

A user switched the daily card on and then nothing ever arrived, with no
explanation. The cron filters out anyone with no deck to draw from — which is
every user until they finish a conversation with Lyra — and returned
skipped_no_deck, which nobody was reading.

It now sends the invitation instead: "you asked for a card each morning, but
there is no deck to draw one from yet", with the CTA pointing at /decks/new
rather than /today.

ONCE. A daily nag about a thing someone has not got round to is worse than the
silence was, so after the first one it goes quiet until a deck exists. The
record is the delivery row itself — an invitation is the only delivery with
neither a deck nor a card against it, and none of the 62 existing rows in
production matches that shape, so nobody is wrongly counted as already invited.

A starter deck was the other option and I did not take it: it costs image
credits on every signup and would hand every new user the sa

fix(prompts): ask the deck writer for an object, not a mood

The last card-art failure, and the one no amount of image-prompt surgery could
reach: when a card's imagePrompt names nothing a painter could point at — "a
swirling vortex of faded parchment and ghostly blueprints, converging at a
misty, indistinct crossroads" — the image model falls back on its own idea of
an oracle card, which is a robed figure. That card failed 2 of 3 even after v3.

Three changes to DECK_GENERATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT:

- Every imagePrompt must OPEN on one concrete physical object. The first eight
  words decide the picture. Mood, light and setting come after it. If a card's
  meaning is abstract, pick a thing that stands for it — the meaning lives in
  the card's text, not in the picture.
- Prefer an object, a plant, an animal or a place over a person or a body part.
  The image pipeline is tuned for uninhabited scenes, so "a pair of weathered
  hands" fights it. Choose the potter's wheel over the potter's hands.

fix(prompts): the app was writing the one word it is not allowed to write

"Journey" is a house rule and no prompt had ever been told about it. On
production: 2 of 15 deck descriptions and 5 of 91 card texts contain it,
including the description on the very first deck a new user is shown —
"Embrace your unfolding journey with wisdom and self-compassion."

HOUSE_VOICE_RULES is appended to every system prompt whose output reaches a
reader: deck generation, the Chronicle conversation and onboarding, journey
card generation, and the reading interpretation. Two prompts were also
instructing the model to use it ("take the seeker on a journey through the
cards"); both rewritten.

Also caps anonymous feedback at 5/hour on a hash of the caller's IP. The
signed-in limit shipped this morning could not see them, and the FAB renders
on the marketing pages, so an unauthenticated script had the table to itself.
